Narathiwat Airport Overwhelmed as Floods Cut Off Hat Yai Access

Narathiwat Airport saw a massive influx of passengers on November 27. This surge was due to travelers from Yala and Patani provinces being unable to reach their scheduled flights at Hat Yai Airport in Songkhla because the connecting routes were completely cut off by flooding.

Among these passengers was a large contingent of foreign nationals from Sri Lanka, India, Bangladesh, the Philippines, and Myanmar. This group had been attending the World Ijtima Thailand 2025 global religious gathering at the Da'wah Center of Thailand in Yala Province between November 20-23 and became stranded.

Some of these travelers had their original flights cancelled. They decided to forfeit their existing tickets and instead traveled to Narathiwat to purchase new tickets to Bangkok. Consequently, all three flights operating between Narathiwat and Bangkok that day were fully booked in both directions. #Narathiwat #Narathiwatairport #thailand #flood

The Philippine Consulate General in Hong Kong continues to coordinate with local authorities to "determine the whereabouts of one [unidentified] missing Filipino," the DFA said.
